proofs.label: L:gaussian-scalar-powers

assertion_checks.reason: Match the same four claims: weighted powers, integer consequence, finite sequence Holder, fractional expectation. No additional theorem or infinite sequence scope is asserted.
For v>0 division gives t^theta<=theta*t+1-theta. With0<theta<1, theta-1<0 makes derivative negative on(0,1),positive on(1,infinity), and value0 at1. Continuity handles t=0; v=0 remains separate.
u=|x|^L,v=|y|^L,theta=q/L is admissible exactly when0<q<L. Resulting exponents q,L-q and weights q/L,(L-q)/L are correct. Unchanged0^0 integer convention covers endpoint identities.

For m>1 the normalized nonnegative entries a,b give u=a^m,v=b^(m/(m-1)); u^(1/m)v^(1-1/m)=ab. Both sums are1 after the nonzero-norm branch, so the weighted sum is1. Multiplying by both original norms restores finite Holder.

For F=E Z finite and positive, (Z/F)^r<=rZ/F+1-r has integrable right side of expectation1. Nonnegative left side is thus integrable, permitting E(Z/F)^r<=1 and multiplication by F^r. F=0 remains Z=0 almost surely. No circular assumption of fractional integrability.

proofs.label: L:gaussian-trace-bounds

assertion_checks.reason: Finite Hermitian Y is diagonalized; B and D are represented in that basis. A unitary representation of D supplies its diagonal entries without simultaneous diagonalization or commutation.

The ith diagonal entry of B Y^q B Y^(L-q) sums b_ij lambda_j^q b_ji lambda_i^(L-q). Hermitian symmetry gives |b_ij|^2; real eigenvalues and integer powers ensure real summands, including negative eigenvalues.

After absolute values, weight q/L multiplies |lambda_j|^L and (L-q)/L multiplies |lambda_i|^L. Swapping finite indices in the first sum preserves |b_ij|^2 by Hermitian symmetry. (B^2)_ii=sum_j|b_ij|^2 identifies both unweighted sums with Tr(B^2|Y|^L); weights sum1. Noncommuting factors are not reordered.

For each i, |U_ij|^2 are nonnegative weights of sum1 with weighted mean d_i. Averaging t^m>=s^m+m*s^(m-1)*(t-s) at s=d_i,t=theta_j cancels the linear term. Summation over i then uses column sums1 for equality with Tr D^m; it does not assert equality in Jensen.

Scalar Holder with conjugates m,m/(m-1) gives (sum d_i^m)^(1/m) and (sum |lambda_i|^(2m))^((m-1)/m), since(2m-2)*m/(m-1)=2m. Positivity of D, m>=2 and zero sums remain exactly as stated. No operator Holder or extra spectral domain is assumed.

proofs.label: P:finite-gaussian-matrix

assertion_checks.reason: Hermitian estimate precedes rectangular dilation, with three matching steps; endpoint m=1 is separate. No stronger moments or dimension/covariance assumptions are introduced.

For fixed other coordinates, standard Gaussian density derivative is -g_k times density. Integrating -P times this derivative by parts gives +partial_k P. Polynomial times Gaussian tends to zero at both infinities. Prior absolute polynomial integrability justifies Fubini; complex polynomials remain treated by real/imaginary parts.
partial_k Y=B_k. Differentiating Y^(2m-1) produces Y^q B_k Y^(L-q),q=0..L,L=2m-2; leading B_k is retained from Tr(B_k Y^(2m-1)). This preserves noncommutative order and exactly2m-1 terms.

assertion_checks.added_passage: Step2 first two inequalities and sums/expectation
assertion_checks.reason: Finite sums and integrable polynomials allow linearity of expectation. Pointwise trace-word bounds sum k to D=sum B_k^2 and q to2m-1. Pointwise scalar trace Holder then permits deterministic (Tr D^m)^(1/m) outside expectation. No eigenbasis random selection/differentiation is required.

Hermitian B_k gives B_k^2>=0, hence D>=0. Tr|Y|^(2m)=Tr Y^(2m)>=0 with finite expectation F. Scalar expectation estimate applies to r=(m-1)/m in(0,1) for m>=2, retaining the correct inequality direction.
F>0 division gives F^(1/m)<=(2m-1)*(Tr D^m)^(1/m). Raising nonnegative sides to m yields(2m-1)^m Tr D^m. F=0 remains separate; no division by Tr D^m or assumption it is positive.
E g_k g_l=0 for k!=l by centering/independence, and E g_k^2=1. Thus E Y^2=sum B_k^2 before trace, proving the equality. No Gaussian higher-moment recursion is substituted.

B_k Hermitian dilation squares to diag(A_k A_k*,A_k* A_k); summed squares give D. Y^2=diag(XX*,X*X); its mth power is Y^(2m) with corresponding powered blocks. All are finite square blocks although o and n may differ.

Rectangular trace cyclicity gives Tr(XX*)^m=Tr(X*X)^m for m>=1. Their sum is2 times Schatten pth power. Substitution into Hermitian estimate divides by2 before p=2m root, yielding sqrt(p-1) and the average of both variance powers. Maximum bound and equality atp=2 are unchanged; no dimensional factor is introduced.
